title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: What is the difference between a workflow and an agent, as the terms are used for systems built around a language model?

options.text: A workflow never calls tools, while an agent is a system that does call tools
In a workflow, code fixes the order of steps; in an agent, the model chooses them
A workflow uses a small model, while an agent always needs the largest model
In a workflow, the model chooses the steps; in an agent, code fixes the order

items.stem: A Python function takes a booking request, always calls the model once to pull out the machine and time, then runs check_calendar in code, then calls the model once more to write a reply. The model never decides whether or when to call a tool. What is this system?

options.text: An agent, because it calls a language model and also runs a tool
An agent, because the model writes the final reply to the student
A workflow, because the code decides the steps and their order
A workflow, because it makes fewer than five calls to the model

items.stem: Your makerspace assistant must book a machine. Every booking needs the same steps in the same order: check the calendar, check the student's training record, then write the booking. Which design is the better choice for this part, and why?

options.text: An agent, because the model may find a cleverer order of the steps
An agent, because a loop is always more accurate than fixed code
A workflow, because the steps are known, so fixed code is cheaper and more predictable
A workflow, because a model cannot be trusted to call any tool at all

items.stem: Your sponsor's budget is counted in model calls. For a booking request, a fixed workflow always makes 2 model calls. An agent handling the same request averages 5 model calls, because it decides step by step and each step is one call. For 1,000 booking requests, how many more model calls does the agent make than the workflow?

Students sometimes ask open questions such as "my 3D print keeps warping, what should I try?" The assistant cannot know in advance which manuals or checks it will need. In one sentence, should this part be a fixed workflow or an agent, and why?
A teammate says, "Any system that uses a language model and tools is an agent." In one or two sentences, correct them: what question decides whether it is a workflow or an agent?
